segments.title: Chương 281: Hỉ sự liên miên
segments.content:
Chapter 285 0282 A Series of Fortunate Events

"President Chen, 'uniquely' isn't pronounced 'U-ni-que-ly,' the stress shouldn't be on the first syllable. It should be like this..."

Chen Guiliang was currently cramming for English, especially practicing his spoken English.

Even if he were in his peak condition from his past life, right after passing the CET-4 exam, his listening and speaking skills were still atrocious. The standard "mute English" of a small-town youth.

He had no choice. For next year's IPO roadshow, Chen Guiliang had to go in person.

Although he could have a translator with him the entire time, a founder who couldn't handle basic communication in English would leave a rather poor impression during the roadshow. Especially the founder of an internet company!

Chen Guiliang still had seven or eight months to practice.

By then, he just needed to be able to handle daily conversations.

As for complex financial issues and professional terminology, that part of the English could be left to other members of the team.

The person currently serving as Chen Guiliang's English tutor was one of the graduate students Professor Wu had brought along to assist with the IPO preparations. These graduate students had all signed non-disclosure agreements, forbidden from revealing any information before the listing.

The lesson was one hour a day, considered English tutoring hired by Chen Guiliang, and he would practice on his own for the rest of the time.

After today's lesson ended, the graduate student said, "President Chen's feel for the language is actually excellent. For the parts you have trouble with, you don't make the same mistake again after one or two corrections. You were just out of practice before and probably never spoke it out loud. Also, you still need to improve your vocabulary..."

"Thank you for your trouble, Mr. Yuan." Chen Guiliang smiled and shook his hand.

The graduate student said, "It's no trouble at all. It's my honor."

Chen Guiliang was spending even less time attending classes now, and he barely even went back to his dorm, having moved into the apartment he had just bought.

It lacked furniture and appliances, but that didn't matter. Chen Guiliang just set up a computer and had an internet line installed. Then he bought some bedding and moved in.

When he got home at night, his main activity was practicing his spoken English in front of a mirror while listening to a language repeater.

And memorizing English words on the side.

He even fell asleep to the sound of English recitations from the language repeater.

This level of diligence felt like he was back in his final year of high school.

It was quite fulfilling.

There were some things Chen Guiliang liked to procrastinate on and muddle through. But once he decided to do something, he would definitely devote himself to doing it well.

He now also enjoyed using a VPN to browse American portal websites, looking up any words he didn't know in an English-Chinese dictionary. This method of learning was far more effective than just memorizing vocabulary lists.

"Huh?"

Chen Guiliang abruptly picked up his English-Chinese dictionary, checking a word on the English portal site.

He had unintentionally seen a major news story that had just been posted: Google had acquired YouTube for a sky-high price of 1.65 billion US dollars!

Chen Guiliang quickly grabbed his phone and called Wang Wei.

"President Chen, it's so late. Are you still busy?" Wang Wei expressed a hint of displeasure. At this hour, he was in the middle of getting intimate with his girlfriend.

Chen Guiliang said, "Google acquired YouTube."

Wang Wei said, "So what if they acquired it? Deals like this are very normal. If it sold for a high price, it would be good news for our Tudou.com."

"Guess what the acquisition price was," Chen Guiliang asked.

Wang Wei thought for a moment and made a bold estimate, "A billion US dollars?"

"1.65 billion!" Chen Guiliang said.

"How much?"

Wang Wei couldn't care less about his girlfriend anymore, springing upright in bed.

Six months ago, when YouTube had its financing round, its post-money valuation was just shy of 500 million US dollars. In just half a year, it had actually sold for the astronomical price of 1.65 billion US dollars.

Wang Wei's imagination had reached its limit, merely doubling the valuation from half a year ago.

Chen Guiliang said, "It is indeed 1.65 billion US dollars."

Wang Wei asked, "Where did you get this news?"

Chen Guiliang said, "I'm browsing an American portal site. It's major news that was just posted. Tudou.com is now the largest site of its kind in China, so we can't give an inch in the next financing round. By the way, ByteDance will also be making an additional investment."

"No problem. Haha, hahaha," Wang Wei started laughing as he spoke.

With YouTube being acquired for a sky-high price, Tudou.com's value would naturally rise, destined to become the focal point of capital pursuit.

Although Tudou.com was a money-losing asset, which would have a negative impact when ByteDance faced its SEC review, it was absolutely positive news for the IPO financing, especially with this move from YouTube.

For the underwriters, they might even place more importance on Tudou.com. Because no matter how much "Quan Yu Tianxia" earned, it was still very unfamiliar to American investors.

The American underwriters could simply point to Tudou.com and say it was the "Chinese YouTube," and in doing so, raise ByteDance's IPO pricing range by a few dollars.

During the roadshow, Chen Guiliang could also go wild hyping up Tudou.com.

The accountants could also re-evaluate ByteDance's equity in Tudou.com at fair value, causing ByteDance's net assets to increase dramatically.

After chatting with Wang Wei, Chen Guiliang called Lu Zhihui, the person in charge of his company's IPO.

Lu Zhihui said as soon as he answered, "President Chen, since it's so late, I was planning to report to you tomorrow. There's major positive news from the US. Google acquired YouTube for the sky-high price of 1.65 billion US dollars!"

"I was just about to tell you the same thing," Chen Guiliang laughed.

Lu Zhihui exclaimed joyfully, "The ancients spoke of favorable timing, geographical advantage, and harmonious human relationships. We've just run into favorable timing. This will absolutely speed up the IPO financing process! A lot of the time, when you tell China's story, those Americans don't get it. For our roadshow, we just need to grab onto two points: ByteDance is benchmarked against Facebook, and Tudou.com is benchmarked against YouTube. If we build our case around these two, they'll like to listen and they'll be able to understand."

"I completely agree with your point of view," Chen Guiliang said.

The two continued their pleasant chat for a few more sentences, deciding to discuss the specifics when they met the next day.

The next day, the investors from the major venture capital firms holding shares in ByteDance all called to offer their congratulations and discuss the series of changes this would trigger.

Those investors were all bullish on Tudou.com and were discussing how to invest more. Those who hadn't invested before now wanted in.

Furthermore, everyone supported ByteDance's additional investment in Tudou.com, working together to make ByteDance's IPO go more smoothly.

China's major portal sites, as well as IT and finance newspapers, also widely reported on Google's massive acquisition of YouTube. This instantly caused UGC video websites like Tudou.com to break out into the mainstream.

Breaking out into the mainstream meant gaining the attention of the entire nation.

One venture capital firm after another began to proactively contact Wang Wei.

Also being contacted were the founders of other video sites like 56.com, 6.cn, and Ku6.com.

Youku, which was still in its trial phase and hadn't officially launched, also became a hot commodity overnight. Although the site didn't have any impressive data, its founder was the former CEO of Sohu.

At that moment, all of China's UGC video websites took a step forward into a new round of financing.

It was particularly frenzied, even crazier than the venture capital craze at the beginning of the year!

Several days later, Chen Guiliang once again convened a board meeting. The main item on the agenda was to finalize the VIE structure, and to discuss the matter of Tudou.com on the side.
